recognize_zh: 視野中四顆嗜中性球的核都沒有正常分成 3–5 葉，而是橢圓、花生形或圓形，染色質非常濃縮成塊，細胞質顆粒正常；多顆同時出現低分葉，符合 Pelger-Huët 異常。
features: Multiple neutrophils of normal size with hyposegmented nuclei
Nuclei oval, peanut-shaped or round (non-segmented), without well-formed lobes
Coarsely clumped, very condensed chromatin indicating nuclear maturity
Pale pink cytoplasm with normal fine granulation
Normochromic red cells with occasional polychromatic cells
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows several neutrophils, all of which display hyposegmented nuclei that are oval, peanut-shaped or round. The nuclear chromatin is coarsely clumped and mature, and the cytoplasm shows normal granulation without hypogranularity. Red cells are largely normochromic with occasional polychromatic cells. Findings are consistent with Pelger-Huët anomaly; review of the entire neutrophil population and family history is needed to separate the inherited anomaly from acquired pseudo-Pelger-Huët change.

ddx.vs: Acquired change usually affects only a subset of neutrophils and is often accompanied by cytoplasmic hypogranularity and other dysplastic or cytopenic features.
Band forms have horseshoe-shaped, non-constricted nuclei with less clumped chromatin rather than compact round or bilobed dense nuclei.
Metamyelocytes have kidney-shaped nuclei with finer chromatin and appear alongside other immature granulocytes.
